status_summary: In March 2026 the White House released President Trump's Cyber Strategy for America (the document shows the month only; a law-firm summary dates it 2026-03-06), which commits to the full suite of defensive and offensive cyber operations, to using all instruments of national power to raise adversaries' costs, and to engaging internationally so that norms and standards reflect US values, but it names neither enforceable or binding norms, the United Nations nor a State Department role. Executive Order 14390, signed 2026-03-06 (91 FR 12051), directs the Secretary of State to press foreign governments to act against cybercrime and fraud networks and to coordinate with allies on consequences, such as limits on foreign assistance, sanctions, visa restrictions and trade penalties, for states that tolerate them; the order does not mention norms. No allied framework of enforceable cyberspace norms was found.

timeline.event: The White House releases President Trump's Cyber Strategy for America (March 2026; the document shows the month only, first of month used, and a law-firm summary reports release on 2026-03-06 alongside EO 14390), committing to the full suite of defensive and offensive cyber operations, to raising adversaries' costs with all instruments of national power, and to international engagement so that norms and standards reflect US values.

Executive Order 14390, Combating Cybercrime, Fraud, and Predatory Schemes Against American Citizens, is signed (published 2026-03-11 at 91 FR 12051), directing the Secretary of State to press foreign governments to act against transnational criminal organizations, to coordinate with allies and partners, and to pursue consequences for tolerating states such as limits on foreign assistance, targeted sanctions, visa restrictions, trade penalties and expulsion of complicit officials.

title: Cyber diplomacy: enforceable norms with allies and help DOD go on offense below conflict
uncertainties: The strategy was read through a fetch of the whitehouse.gov PDF that appeared complete (introduction, six pillars and conclusion); it does not mention enforceable or binding norms, the State Department or the United Nations, and shows only March 2026 as its date, so the 2026-03-06 day rests on a law-firm summary. EO 14390 (91 FR 12051, document 2026-04826) was read in full; outputs of its 60-day review and 120-day action plan were not found. The Pall Mall Process, any allied binding framework, the offensive-cyber presidential memorandum and a reported offensive cyber appropriation were not confirmed. An advocacy group's explainer reports that the UN General Assembly established a non-binding Global Mechanism on ICT security on 2025-12-01 after the open-ended working group's July 2025 report; this is a UN action and is not a timeline event. A news site reported on 2025-04-22 that State's reorganization moved the Bureau of Cyberspace and Digital Policy under the Economic Growth office; the effective date and current placement were not confirmed, so it is not a timeline event. Searches on the US position at the UN mechanism returned no US statement.
